actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species can be found in the Coastal Plain of southeastern the United States of America from southeastern Virginia to Florida and into eastern Louisiana.
documentation.population: The total adult population size for this species is unknown, but is thought to surely exceed 10,000 and might exceed 100,000 individuals (NatureServe 2020). The population trends is unknown.
documentation.habitats: This species can be found in swamps, bayous, margins of muddy sloughs, cypress heads, drainage ditches, sluggish streams, wet meadows, muddy lakes; soft substrate for burrowing or thick aquatic vegetation important for shelter. Often uses crayfish burrows. It may leave water, especially on rainy nights; sometimes found under objects at water's edge. Eggs are laid under objects in damp place near water's edge or possibly in shallow water, or underground. This species has a free-living larval stage. Individuals were found in drainage ditches, suggesting at least a degree of tolerance to habitat degradation.
documentation.threats: Widespread loss of wetlands for agricultural development undoubtedly has eliminated many local subpopulations, but the species remains common in many other areas (Petranka 1998). Despite being found in the international pet trade, it is unknown if current levels constitute a major threat to the species.
documentation.measures:
Conservation Actions In-Place
This species likely occurs in several protected areas.

Conservation Needed
Improved habitat protection and site management, particularly of coastal plain wetlands, is recommended.

Research Needed
Further research on this species' distribution, population size and trends is recommended.
documentation.use_trade: This species has international commercial value in the pet trade, but no national commercial value.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution and presumed large population.
